key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE simulations reveal a shift from localized, phonon-like Li⁺ motion below 500 K to contrasting high-temperature dynamics near 800 K, with strong Li⁺–framework competition at 500–700 K.
engineering_relevance: Understanding temperature-dependent coupling between lithium and framework motion can inform the design of solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries.
method: Run molecular dynamics of argyrodite Li₆PS₅Cl using a fine-tuned MACE interatomic potential.
Analyze collective ion motion through essential dynamics, eigenspectra, and low-dimensional embeddings.
Use Langevin dynamics to test how damping framework motion affects Li⁺ dynamics.
evidence_signal: Eigenspectra and projected embeddings show nonmonotonic temperature dependence at 500–700 K, with framework-damping simulations supporting competition between Li⁺ and framework dynamics.
watch_item: The abstract does not report quantitative model-accuracy benchmarks or experimental validation, limiting assessment of predictive reliability.
paper_title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
